newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tigers overrun Sri Lankan military base, 11 killed.
newsitem.headline: Tigers overrun Sri Lankan military base, 11 killed.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas struck back at Sri Lankan forces on Thursday with pre-dawn attacks on two bases in the island's east, killing 11 military personnel and wounding 74, military officials said.
A military spokesman said four rebel fighters were killed and many wounded.
The guerrillas overran a small army camp in eastern Batticaloa district early on Thursday and attacked an air force base in Trincomalee district, badly damaging a transport plane, the officials said.

The attacks came after troops last month captured a highway linking two army-controlled towns in the north of the island with little opposition from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels who held large areas to the south and southwest.

A military spokesman told Reuters one airman was killed, four were wounded and a Chinese-made Y-12 transport plane was damaged when rebels attacked China Bay air force base in eastern Trincomalee, some 240 km (150 miles) from the capital Colombo.
Earlier reports had said four air force men were killed.
Trincomalee police said about 300 rebels attacked the China Bay base with mortars and rocket launchers late on Wednesday.
Military officials said a small group of rebels and suicide bombers had infiltrated the camp, which had come under heavy mortar fire that set the aircraft ablaze.

They also said some 500 rebels had overrun Vaunathivu camp in Batticaloa district, some 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo. Reinforcements that reached the camp almost 12 hours after the attack began found the bodies of 10 soldiers.
"The camp was overrun. The situation is not good," said an army official. "The death toll could rise. The LTTE blew up a bridge to delay reinforcements."
More than 70 soldiers were wounded in the raid, he added.
The military spokesman said there were many LTTE casualties in the China Bay attack, which began at about 11.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) and lasted three hours.
"Four terrorist suicide bombers were killed and a large number of them wounded," the spokesman said. "The terrorists withdrew after we launched ground and air attacks."
Rebel communications monitored by the army indicated the LTTE were seeking urgent medical aid for the wounded, he said.
An LTTE spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment.
Last year, the LTTE overran an important army base on the northeast coast, killing or capturing the camp's 1,000 men and dealing the the military its worst blow in the 13-year war.
In January, the rebels again attacked a military base at Paranthan, a key road junction south of Jaffna. The army said 223 soldiers died and the rebels said they lost at least 140.
But the military faced little resistence last month when troops backed by artillery, tanks and air cover moved westwards from northern Vavuniya to link up with forces in Mannar.

The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese island's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the civil war, but the LTTE says the number is higher.
